decisions.reason: The connector pinout uses logical signal names SCL0 and 5V_EN; remapping those signals at the ESP32 does not change their connector positions or labels.
The GPIO remapping does not change the separate interboard power connector or its matching-pin-order rule.
Moving SCL0 to another MCU GPIO does not change the retained I2C speed, cable length, pull-ups, or series-resistor conditioning.
The source changes 5V_EN, SCL0, and SPI MOSI GPIO assignments but does not change the USB D+ and D- interface.
The necessary change from GPIO3 to GPIO5 is already represented by the candidate's message-291 MODIFY event.
The GPIO reassignment does not alter the three-board architecture or the roles of the main and sensor boards.
The GPIO remapping does not change the standalone USB regulator, its activation condition, powered loads, or source-selection behavior.
The candidate explicitly records GPIO3 as the control for the 5V_EN-based LED rail shutdown, so assigning 5V_EN to GPIO5 necessarily updates that control description.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Apologies, GPIO3 came from my original ESP32 design, so that was my mistake. You can assign 5V_EN to GPIO5. I also noticed that the WROOM-1 module does not expose GPIO22, 23, 25, or 27, so I need to remap SCL0 (GPIO22→38) and SPI MOSI (GPIO23→26). I will revise the documentation and send you the complete updated GPIO table.

value_updates.led_power_control: GPIO5-controlled shutdown of the complete 5V rail when the LEDs are unnecessary

decisions.reason: The MCU GPIO remapping does not change the sensor board's role as a connector hub.
Assigning SPI MOSI to GPIO26 conflicts with the candidate's existing GPIO26 touch-wake assignment, but the source does not decide whether the touch-wake input or SPI MOSI should be remapped.
The GPIO mapping change does not alter the requirement for an eight-LED array board.
The GPIO reassignment does not change the AXP2101 power source, required rails, or battery power path.
